title: SOC Security Jobs: 3 Roles, CISA, and Evidence Work Employers Want
summary: Explore three SOC compliance roles, employer expectations, CISA certification rules, NICE role mapping, and how automated evidence workflows shape hiring.
body_markdown:
SOC security jobs are compliance and assurance roles, including SOC auditors, compliance analysts, and program managers, focused on keeping an organization audit-ready and demonstrating control effectiveness to customers and auditors. The three roles worth targeting are SOC compliance analyst, SOC auditor or assurance specialist, and SOC program manager, with evidence coordinator as a common entry point. The fastest realistic route pairs hands-on evidence-collection experience with a plan to qualify for the CISA certification.


---


> **TL;DR:**
>
>
> - Search postings for control testing, trust services criteria, readiness assessments, or SOC support; these terms point to compliance work, not incident response.
> - Entry roles rarely require CISA; earning it requires five years of qualifying experience, though education or other certifications can waive up to three years.
> - A focused plan can prepare you for entry level roles in three to six months; build sample evidence and seek internal audit or controls projects.
> - Employers increasingly expect familiarity with continuous monitoring and automated evidence workflows, including centralized libraries, system integrations, approval chains, and customer facing trust centers.

## Core Roles and Daily Responsibilities in SOC Compliance


Job postings use inconsistent titles for what is often the same work, so it helps to know what each role actually does before you apply.


- **SOC compliance analyst** : gathers evidence for control testing, tracks remediation items, and maintains the mapping between controls and the trust services criteria.
- **SOC auditor or assurance specialist** : performs walkthroughs, tests control design and operating effectiveness, and drafts findings that feed into the final report.
- **SOC program manager** : owns the audit calendar, coordinates with internal teams and external auditors, and reports status to leadership.
- **Evidence coordinator** : a frequent entry-level title, responsible for collecting, organizing, and timestamping artifacts auditors will request.


When you read a posting, look for phrases like "control testing," "trust services criteria," "readiness assessment," or "SOC 1/SOC 2 support." Those phrases signal compliance and assurance work rather than a technical security operations role. Postings that mention SOX, ITGCs (information technology general controls), or GRC (governance, risk, and compliance) tooling also belong in this category. A quick checklist: if the description talks about reports, auditors, and evidence rather than incident response or threat detection, you are looking at a SOC compliance position worth pursuing.


## Skills, Experience, and Certifications Hiring Managers Expect


Hiring managers for SOC compliance roles look for a mix of technical fluency and communication skill, since the job sits between engineering teams and external auditors.


- **ITGCs and control testing** : understanding access provisioning, change management, and logging controls well enough to test them.
- **Evidence collection** : knowing what a defensible audit trail looks like for each control.
- **Trust services criteria familiarity** : security, availability, processing integrity, confidentiality, and privacy, as defined in[AICPA's SOC 2 reporting guidance](https://www.aicpa-cima.com/cpe-learning/publication/soc-2-reporting-on-an-examination-of-controls-at-a-service-organization-relevant-to-security-availability-processing-integrity-confidentiality-or-privacy) .
- **Stakeholder communication** : translating audit findings into language engineering and leadership teams can act on.


Certification expectations are more specific than most career guides admit. **ISACA requires[five years of qualifying professional experience](https://www.isaca.org/credentialing/cisa) in information systems auditing, control, assurance, or security work to earn the CISA credential, though up to three years can be waived with qualifying education or other certifications.** That waiver matters if you are coming from an adjacent field like internal audit or IT, since it can shorten your timeline to eligibility by years.


> The NICE Framework defines Work Roles as a set of Task statements tied to specific Knowledge and Skill statements, giving jobseekers a shared vocabulary for matching their background to employer expectations.


Using[NIST's NICE Framework](https://www.nist.gov/itl/applied-cybersecurity/nice/nice-framework-resource-center/getting-started) to map your own experience against published Task, Knowledge, and Skill (TKS) statements is a practical way to translate scattered audit or IT experience into language that matches how employers write job descriptions.


## How to Break Into SOC Compliance Jobs: a Practical Roadmap


Breaking in is less about credentials alone and more about showing you understand how evidence moves through an audit cycle.


1. **Map your background to a NICE work role.** Identify which published Task and Knowledge statements already match your experience, even if your title never said "compliance."
2. **Build a personal evidence repository.** Collect sample control descriptions, sanitized evidence artifacts, and a mock SOC 2 readiness checklist you can speak to in interviews.
3. **Get hands-on through internal audit or advisory projects.** Volunteer for a SOX walkthrough, a vendor risk review, or an internal controls project if your current role allows it.
4. **Start the CISA clock early.** Confirm which of your prior roles count toward the five-year requirement and whether a waiver applies, then register for the exam once your timeline is clear.
5. **Apply with evidence-focused stories.** Frame resume bullets around outcomes: "Reduced evidence-collection cycle from three weeks to five days by building a centralized control repository" lands harder than "Assisted with SOC 2 audit."


Short-term projects that build credibility fast include drafting a sample control walkthrough document, assembling a mock evidence package for a single trust services criterion, or shadowing a readiness assessment at your current employer.


**Pro Tip:** *Keep a running log of every control you've tested or evidence artifact you've organized, even informally. It becomes both interview material and a head start on your CISA experience verification.*


## Career Progression, Senior Roles, and What Accelerates Promotion


Progression in SOC compliance tends to follow a predictable arc: evidence coordinator or junior analyst, then SOC compliance analyst, then senior analyst or auditor, then program manager or advisory consultant.


- **Cross-functional SOX or IT audit experience** signals you can handle broader control environments, not just one framework.
- **GRC tooling fluency** (platforms used to track controls, risks, and remediation) is increasingly a baseline expectation rather than a differentiator.
- **Control design experience** , not just testing, shows you can help a team build controls that pass audit the first time.
- **Comfort with continuous monitoring** is now part of senior expectations, since many organizations have moved away from point-in-time evidence pulls toward ongoing control validation.


Advisory and consulting positions, often the next step after a few years in an in-house compliance role, typically expect multi-year experience and fluency across SOC 1, SOC 2, SOX, and frameworks like COBIT or ISO 27000. For a closer look at how SOC reporting itself is structured, our breakdown of[SOC 2 Type 1 vs Type 2 differences](https://blog.skypher.co/blog/soc-2-type-1-vs-type-2-differences) is a useful reference when you are prepping for interviews that assume you know the distinction cold.


## How Automation Reshapes SOC Compliance Work


The day-to-day of SOC compliance has shifted from manual evidence chasing toward continuous monitoring and automated questionnaire response, and hiring managers increasingly expect candidates to understand both.


- **Evidence-library curation** : maintaining a centralized, pre-vetted set of policies and artifacts that can be reused across audits and customer questionnaires.
- **Integration familiarity** : knowing how evidence flows between systems like ticketing tools, identity providers, and GRC platforms.
- **Workflow orchestration** : understanding how automated reminders and approval chains keep evidence current between audit cycles.
- **Trust Center maintenance** : keeping a customer-facing summary of your security posture accurate and current, a concept worth citing directly on a resume.


**Pro Tip:** *If you've maintained or contributed to a security knowledge base or evidence repository, name the tools and update cadence on your resume. Specificity here reads as real operational experience, not a buzzword.*


## Hiring Manager Priorities and Realistic Timelines


Across the postings and frameworks we track, hiring managers consistently prioritize demonstrable evidence work over credentials alone: a candidate who can describe a real control walkthrough beats one who only lists certifications. A realistic timeline for an entry-level SOC compliance role is three to six months of focused preparation, while qualifying for the CISA exam often takes one to three years depending on prior experience and available waivers. Start your evidence repository now, even before you have a title that requires one.


> *— Gaspard*


## FAQ


### What is the difference between a SOC auditor and a compliance analyst?


A SOC auditor tests control design and operating effectiveness and drafts formal findings, while a compliance analyst focuses on gathering and organizing the evidence those tests rely on. In smaller organizations, one person often does both.


### Do I need a CISA certification to get an entry-level SOC compliance job?


No, most entry-level roles like evidence coordinator or junior compliance analyst do not require CISA. ISACA requires five years of qualifying experience for the credential, so it is typically a mid-career goal rather than an entry requirement.


### What industries hire the most SOC compliance professionals?


Technology and software companies hire heavily for these roles because they frequently undergo SOC 2 examinations for enterprise customers, and financial services firms hire similarly due to vendor risk requirements. Healthcare, insurance, and any B2B company handling sensitive customer data also maintain active compliance teams.


### How do questionnaire automation tools change what employers expect from candidates?


Employers increasingly value candidates who can maintain a centralized evidence library and understand how automated tools pull and update that evidence for audits and customer questionnaires. Familiarity with a platform like our[Questionnaire Automation Tool](https://www.skypher.co/) demonstrates you understand modern, efficient evidence workflows rather than only manual processes.


### How does SOC compliance work overlap with IT and legal teams?


Compliance analysts regularly pull evidence from IT teams for access controls and change management, and coordinate with legal on contract language tied to SOC reports. Program managers typically own these relationships and keep audit timelines aligned across departments.
